items.title: California, Napa Valley Premium Wines Sold Under Affordable Labels
items.author: Judy Lagrou
items.content: <article>Oenophiles on beer budgets have never had it better.</article>

items.title: BofA’s Subramanian Says Bonds in Rare Competition With Stocks
items.author: Matt Clinch, Guy Johnson, Anna Edwards and Tom Mackenzie
items.content: <article>Equity markets face a genuine rival in bonds for the first time in decades, according to Savita Subramanian at Bank of America Corp., who also cautioned that elevated investor sentiment leaves stocks more exposed to disappointment than upside.</article>

items.title: Moubarak: GCC Economies Set for Strong Recovery in 2027
items.content: <article>The US-Iran conflict continues to weigh heavily on economies around the world and in particular those in the Gulf. Ramona Moubarak, the MENA Country Risk Head for BMI, a Fitch Solutions Company, spoke to Bloomberg’s Jennifer Zabasajja on Horizons Middle East & Africa as the war enters its 8th month. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rupee Nears Record Low as RBI Hike Leaves Traders Wanting More
items.author: Pratigya Vajpayee
items.content: <article>India’s rupee retreated even after the central bank hiked interest rates for the first time in four years, as the lack of more aggressive steps to tighten liquidity and support the currency left traders disappointed.</article>

items.title: BofA Says Bonds May Outperform Stocks in Next Decade
items.content: <article>"Bonds actually look interesting again," says Savita Subramanian, Bank of America’s head of US equity and quantitative strategy, as she weighs the potential returns from bonds and equities over the next decade. "The risk-return for a 10-year Treasury today is about over 5%," Subramanian tells Bloomberg Television. "Whereas when you look at the S&P 500, our valuation framework suggests that returns over the next ten years might not even be at those levels, at that 5% clip." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: RWE Sees Limited Role in Uniper After Making Joint Bid With KKR
items.author: Eva Brendel
items.content: <article>RWE AG has played down the prospect of taking a major role in state-owned Uniper SE, after the utility teamed up with private equity firm KKR & Co. to make a non-binding bid for the German company.</article>

items.title: India Regulator Presses Jane Street to Respond After Data Share
items.author: Ranjani Raghavan and Shruti Mahajan
items.content: <article>India’s markets regulator told a local court that it has shared with Jane Street Group LLC the trade logs it relied upon for its preliminary order against the Wall Street trader, pressing the firm to respond to the accusations of market manipulation.</article>

items.title: Spanish Miner Abenojar Tungsten Announces Plans for London IPO
items.author: Pablo Mayo Cerqueiro
items.content: <article>Abenojar Tungsten SA announced plans for an initial public offering in London, the latest overseas company to explore a UK listing.</article>

items.title: Hong Kong, Singapore Pitch Rival Gold Hubs to Bullion Market
items.author: Yihui Xie
items.content: <article>Officials from Hong Kong and Singapore pitched rival plans to create gold trading hubs in Asia, underscoring fierce competition to secure new business and capitalize on strong demand for the precious metal.</article>

items.title: Africa’s Ratings Agency Faces Credibility Test in Niche Market
items.author: Kamlesh Bhuckory
items.content: <article>Africa’s new home-grown rating agency must convince investors that it won’t be prone to local bias as it opens its doors for business.</article>

items.title: Euro Falls to 16-Month Low Versus Pound on France’s Fiscal Risks
items.author: Masaki Kondo and Ran Li
items.content: <article>The euro dropped to its lowest against the pound since June last year, weighed down by concerns over France’s deepening fiscal crisis and fresh political risks in the region.</article>

items.title: HSBC Said to Eye Job Cuts in Wealth Management Unit
items.content: <article>HSBC is planning sweeping job cuts across its UK wealth management business as part of a broader push to use artificial intelligence to serve affluent clients more efficiently, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Bloomberg's Tom Metcalf has more. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Athletic Brewing’s Push to Reshape Beer
items.content: <article>Athletic Brewing helped move non-alcoholic beer into the mainstream. Chief Executive Officer Bill Shufelt explains how it paired a reinvented product with the concepts of craft and wellness. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Volkswagen Sets Aside £725 Million for UK Car Finance Payout
items.author: Jamie Nimmo and Upmanyu Trivedi
items.content: <article>The UK financing arm of Volkswagen AG has made a £725 million ($960 million) provision to cover the costs of a plan to compensate British customers who were overcharged for car loans.</article>

items.title: Partners Group Gets Creative to Fix Funds Hit by Redemptions
items.author: Leonard Kehnscherper and Noele Illien
items.content: <article>The Swiss asset manager which pioneered private capital’s push to tap individuals is getting creative again — this time spurred by a wave of clients who want their money back.</article>

items.title: Dutch Government Plans to Halve ABN Amro Stake to 10.5%
items.author: Sarah Jacob and Stephen Carroll
items.content: <article>The Netherlands plans to cut its stake in ABN Amro Bank NV in half, taking the bank closer to full private ownership.</article>

items.title: Japan Index to Slash Hundreds of Stocks to Lure Investors
items.author: Kentaro Tsutsumi
items.content: <article>Japan Exchange Group Inc. unveiled the biggest-ever reshuffle of the Topix on Wednesday, a revamp that shrinks one of Asia’s broadest major equity benchmarks and intensifies pressure on Japanese companies to boost their market appeal.</article>

items.title: Stocks Rally Stalls as Hormuz Attacks Lift Oil: Markets Wrap
items.author: Andre Janse van Vuuren
items.content: <article>A rally in stocks came to a halt and global bonds fell as mounting attacks on tankers in the Middle East pushed oil prices higher.</article>

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 7
items.author: Kanoko Matsuyama and Charles Gorrivan
items.content: <article>Oil rose in choppy trading as traders weighed a pickup in Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz against resilient flows from the Middle East.</article>

items.title: Traders Reload Bets on Higher US Yields After Brief Jolt
items.author: Edward Bolingbroke
items.content: <article>Traders extended their short bets against US government bonds, signaling the selloff that has taken long-term yields to near a 24-year high has room to continue.</article>
